title: Gravitational memory, spin memory and S-duality at null infinity of the heterotic string
abstract: We determine the asymptotic structure at future null infinity of heterotic string theory compactified on $T^6$, in the consistent truncation to the Einstein-frame metric, the axion--dilaton $\tau=a+ie^{-2\phi}$ and the gauge fields descending from ten dimensions, through first order in $\alpha'$. Three results stand out. First, the radiative data, balance laws and memory observables organize under the S-duality group of the four-dimensional theory: the scalar flux in the Bondi mass loss is the invariant metric of $SL(2,\mathbb R)/U(1)$ evaluated on the scalar news, the gauge flux is the norm of a self-dual radiation field, and at fixed vacuum the residual duality rotation acts with charges $0$, $1$ and $2$ on gravitational, electromagnetic and dilaton--axion radiation, so that S-dual processes share their gravitational waveform and memories and differ in their scalar memory. Second, the spin memory receives a gauge-field contribution whose ordinary part is fixed by the Dirac--Schwinger--Zwanziger product of the total charge with the change of the charge aspect; it is generated by mutually nonlocal dyons, and its dipole part agrees in magnitude and sign with the angular momentum radiated by a charge scattered off a magnetic monopole. Third, within the four-derivative effective action, the Gauss--Bonnet and Pontryagin couplings fixed by the Green--Schwarz mechanism leave the mass-loss and angular-momentum balance laws unchanged at first order in $\alpha'$ and first enter the evolution of the spin-two curvature coefficient, $\partial_u\Psi_0^0\supset\tfrac{3i\alpha'}{2}\tau_1\bar\Psi_4^0$, which combines dilaton and axion into the complex scalar charge aspect and is not invariant under the residual duality rotation. For black holes with fixed physical charges $\tau_1$ is of order one, so this is a first-order effect in $\alpha'/M^2$.

title: New Agegraphic Dark Energy in Braneworld Cosmology: A Higher Dimensional Perspective on Dark Energy Evolution
abstract: In this study, we investigate the new agegraphic dark energy model within the context of braneworld cosmology. A higher dimensional viewpoint on the evolution of dark energy is examined. A combination of cold dark matter and dark energy, is explored within the frameworks of RS-II and DGP brane as the underlying gravitational theories. Both the possibilities involving interaction and non-interaction between dark energy and cold dark matter are investigated. A range of cosmological parameters, including the equation of state parameter, deceleration parameter, and statefinder parameters, are examined. The squared velocity of sound is examined to assess the system's stability. A data analysis based on observations, utilizing contemporary cosmological data and the Markov chain Monte Carlo method, is conducted to constrain the parameter space of the model. Our research suggests that the interplay between higher-dimensional phenomena and agegraphic dark energy provides a theoretically robust and observationally consistent framework for the universe's late-time acceleration.

title: The Mechanics of Curvature Inflation
abstract: We examine slow roll directly in the Jordan-frame Hubble equation. For the quadratic Starobinsky action, this equation has an exact mechanical form. Comparing nearby solutions at the same Hubble value gives a local contraction law on the expanding branch with decreasing Hubble rate. A signed square root of the Hubble parameter also continues the vacuum background smoothly through its Hubble zeroes. For metric actions built from a smooth function of the Ricci scalar, coefficients depending only on the Hubble parameter require a derivative expansion. We derive the terms through cubic order and test both the equation residual and the error accumulated by an independently evolved approximation. A regularized inverse-logarithmic extension provides a nontrivial example. On the parameter slice studied, we prove a positive lower bound on the second curvature derivative of the action and compare separate Jordan- and Einstein-frame integrations. The third-order approximation reproduces the exact inflationary trajectory more accurately than the second-order approximation over the interval tested. We also compute the linear scalar and tensor spectra with numerical convergence checks. The benchmark gives a scalar spectral index of 0.97384 and a tensor-to-scalar ratio of 0.00527, evaluated 60 exact Einstein-frame e-folds before the first acceleration exit. These values depend on the chosen action and reference event. The mechanical form supplies approximation tests for the background; the scalaron and its perturbations follow from the original gravitational action.
